user.title: HyperPasscode
user.description:
Codes live in Home Assistant rather than inside a lock, so one policy engine can govern any credential and authorise any action.

There is nothing to configure here. Add your first scope once setup finishes.

error.code_collision: That code is already in use. Two identical codes would make the audit log unattributable.
error.weak_code: That code was rejected as weak. Turn off 'Reject weak codes' in the integration settings to allow it.

user.title: Add code
user.description:
Leave the code blank to have one generated. It is shown on the next step only if you tick 'Keep code viewable'.

Validity dates, use limits, the re-entry grace period and notes are entities on the code's own device once it exists, so they can be changed from a dashboard or an automation.

data_description.name: What this code is for, such as Cleaner or Grocery delivery.
data_description.scope_ids: The scopes this code opens. A code with no scope cannot be used anywhere yet.
data_description.keep_viewable: Stores the code in clear text so it can be read back from the code's device and shared again. Decide now: without it the code is never shown -- not even on the next step -- and can only be regenerated.
data_description.owner: The person this code belongs to. Their name then appears in the audit log and in automations.
data_description.schedule_entities: Schedule helpers that must all be on. These recur weekly, so pair them with the code's 'Valid from' and 'Valid until' entities for a date range.
data_description.condition_entities: Any on/off entities that must all be on. Point one at a calendar to make the code live only during matching events.

created.title: Code created
created.description:
The code for {label} is:

**{code}**

You ticked 'Keep code viewable', so a copy is kept in clear: the code stays readable on this code's own device, under its 'Code' entity. Press Submit to save it.

created_hidden.title: Code created
created_hidden.description:
The code for {label} is:

**{code}**

You left 'Keep code viewable' off, so only a hashed lookup of the code is stored and it is not shown -- not here, and not on the code's device, where 'Store method' will read *hashed*. If you need to read this code back later, cancel and add it again with 'Keep code viewable' ticked.

Press Submit to save it.

reconfigure.title: Edit code
reconfigure.description:
Leave the code blank to keep the existing one. Use counts and history are unaffected by changes here.

Validity dates, use limits, the re-entry grace period and notes live on this code's device, not in this dialog.

data_description.code: Leave empty to keep the current code.
data_description.schedule_entities: Schedule helpers that must all be on.
data_description.condition_entities: Any on/off entities that must all be on.

user.title: Add scope
user.description:
A scope is something codes are entered against, such as a front door, a gate or an alarm. It becomes a device with its own entities.

Code length, inter-key timeout, the terminator keys and the lockout settings all live on that device, so they can be tuned without coming back here.

data_description.default_actions: Run whenever a valid code is entered here, so the common case needs no automation at all.

reconfigure.title: Edit scope
reconfigure.description: Changes take effect immediately. Lockout counters and any half-typed code are left alone.

data_description.default_actions: Run whenever a valid code is entered here.

data_description.code: Never shown again once submitted, and never echoed back into this field.
data_description.source: Which input a credential restricted with "allowed sources" should be judged as coming from.
data_description.dry_run: On, the code is only checked. Turn it off and this really submits: the use is counted, a failure counts towards the lockout that protects your keypad, and the scope's actions run.

data.log_failed_plaintext: Log what was typed on failure

data_description.reject_weak_codes: Refuses repeated digits, sequential runs and well-known codes, for typed codes as well as generated ones.

data_description.per_credential_entities: Gives every credential its own use counter, switches, validity dates and use limits. Turn this off if you have many credentials, or the entity list becomes unusable -- but with it off those settings are only reachable through actions.
data_description.audit_log_size: How many submissions to keep. Every submission also fires an event, so history is kept by the recorder regardless.
data_description.log_failed_plaintext: Off by default: a failed attempt is usually a typo of a real code, so recording it would leak that code into your logs.

code_history_not_purged.title: A discarded code may still be in the recorder database
code_history_not_purged.description:
The stored copy of the code for {label} was discarded, but its recorded history on `{entity_id}` could not be deleted, so the code in clear may remain in the recorder database until that history is purged.

To clear it by hand, call the `recorder.purge_entities` action on `{entity_id}` with `keep_days: 0`. The integration log has the underlying error.
